_schema: {symbol: {date YYYY-MM-DD, verdict: disruptor (its innovation is creating a new, largely untapped market) | innovating (gains from a changing trend) | neutral | threatened (a trend or new tech could make its core business obsolete) | disrupted (that is already happening), summary: one line, threats: [the trend / technology / competitor that could make it obsolete], innovation: [the new or untapped market it is creating, with a size or adoption fact if known], sources: [urls], by: routine or session}}. Written via disruption.save_note(). Ignored after 90 days. Moves the quant label at most one step.

ABNB.summary: AI concierge/agentic app and AI support (40%+ issues resolved) defend traffic; chatbot referrals convert better than Google. Services/experiences still tiny and growth slowed ~40% (2022) to ~10% (2025), so the new-market claim is unproven.
threats: LLM/agentic trip planners (OpenAI, Google) could own discovery and turn Airbnb into a supply backend
growth deceleration
innovation: AI-first concierge app
Services and Experiences categories (small share of bookings)

ADBE.summary: AI-native image/video generators and design tools (Figma, Canva, Midjourney, Google/OpenAI models) lower the value of pro creative software; Adobe answers with Firefly and partner models, growth slowed to ~13%. Pressure is real but revenue still rising.
threats: AI-native generators (Midjourney, OpenAI, Google)
Figma, Canva
innovation: Firefly commercially-safe models, 70M+ freemium AI MAU

AEM.summary: Senior gold miner; 2026 guide 3.3-3.5Moz at AISC $1,400-1,550 held, capex raised for Hope Bay; no technology substitute for mined gold, results track the gold price.
threats: gold price / cost inflation (fuel), not obsolescence
innovation: Hope Bay build, Finnish acquisitions: 20-30% production growth target over a decade

AFRM.summary: BNPL keeps taking share of card spend (Amazon renewal, JPMorgan merchant tie-up); not obsolescence, but Klarna competition is real (Walmart switched to Klarna) and funding debt is rising.
threats: Klarna and other BNPL lenders competing for merchant exclusives (Walmart moved to Klarna)
rising funding debt ($2.4B)
innovation: pay-over-time at checkout displacing credit cards; Amazon contract renewed, JPMorgan merchant partnership

ALAB.summary: Gains from the shift to rack-scale AI servers and is pushing into in-rack switching (Scorpio X), a market Nvidia NVLink and Broadcom also contest.
threats: Nvidia NVLink/NVLink Fusion
Broadcom in-rack switching
customer concentration
innovation: Scorpio X 320-lane switch ramping 2H26 (company sees a $20B market by 2030)
Aries 7 PCIe 7
Orion rack architecture

AM.summary: Gas gathering/water midstream tied to one customer (Antero Resources); no technology is making it obsolete, and it creates no new market. Q3 2026 EPS $0.28 vs $0.35 est, curtailments ~10 Bcf with 15-20 Bcf expected in Q4.
threats: single-customer dependence on Antero Resources volumes; gas curtailments when prices are weak

AMAT.summary: Broadest equipment maker, gains from AI chip demand, but Mizuho expects it to lag the WFE market as Chinese rivals (AMEC, Naura) win domestic share in core tools; date of that note is unclear, so evidence is thin.
threats: Chinese competitors in etch/deposition (Mizuho)
innovation: Tools for gate-all-around and advanced packaging

AMD.summary: Gains from the AI-compute shift: OpenAI 6 GW MI450 deal (first 1 GW from 2H26) plus Meta as a customer, Helios rack-scale systems, and continued CPU share gains from Intel. Still a distant No. 2 to Nvidia in accelerators.
threats: Nvidia's lead in AI accelerators and software (CUDA)
Custom ASICs from hyperscalers
innovation: MI450/Helios rack-scale AI systems
EPYC server share gains

AMZN.summary: AWS grew 28% last quarter and Trainium is reported at a ~$20B annual pace with large Anthropic/OpenAI commitments; Amazon gains from the AI-compute shift rather than being displaced by it.
threats: low-cost retail rivals and offline/local retailers (BofA risk list)
Nvidia/GPU alternatives competing with Trainium
innovation: custom AI silicon (Trainium 3 in 2026) sold through AWS

ANET.summary: Nvidia's Spectrum-X Ethernet switches, bundled with its GPUs and already used by Meta and Oracle, threaten Arista's pricing power; Arista still leads data-center switching and the threat is not yet in its results.
threats: Nvidia Spectrum-X bundled with GPUs (Meta, Oracle)
NVLink proprietary in-rack links
dependence on Broadcom switch chips
innovation: entering in-rack (scale-up) switching
open co-packaged optics, samples next year

ARGX.summary: Vyvgart built the FcRn-blocker market (gMG, CIDP) and still leads it; the Oct 8 Sjogren's futility stop removes one expansion, not the core franchise. FB102 celiac Phase 2 hit its endpoint.
threats: competing FcRn blockers (J&J nipocalimab, UCB)
failed indication expansions (Sjogren's halted 2026-10-08)
innovation: FcRn blockade across autoimmune diseases
FB102 (CD122) in celiac disease

ARM.summary: Arm-based hyperscaler CPUs are displacing x86 servers (data-center royalties reportedly more than doubled in FY2026) and Arm now sells its own data-center CPU; RISC-V is a long-term threat, strongest in low-cost embedded chips.
threats: RISC-V open instruction set (long-term, cost-sensitive segments)
channel conflict / FTC scrutiny from selling its own chips
innovation: Arm server CPUs replacing x86 in data centers
own AGI data-center CPU (Meta first customer)

ASML.summary: Sole supplier of EUV lithography; the AI chip build-out needs it. Risk is pace, not obsolescence: TSMC reportedly defers High-NA EUV (~$400M/tool) to 2029+, while Intel, Samsung and SK hynix adopt sooner.
threats: Customer pushback on High-NA EUV cost; TSMC deferring adoption (timing risk, no substitute technology named)
innovation: High-NA EUV: first production chips expected in 2026 (CEO, May 2026); Intel production milestone

ASND.summary: Yorvipath (hypoparathyroidism) revenue ~EUR252M in Q2 2026, 6,300+ US patient enrollments, launches in 35+ countries; TransCon pipeline extends it. Single-product concentration is the risk.
innovation: TransCon long-acting prodrug platform
Yorvipath

AU.summary: Gold producer: revenue follows the gold price; Q2 cash costs up 21% to $1,480/oz on inflation and gold-linked royalties, H2 output guided ~6% higher with lower unit costs. No technology obsolescence angle.
threats: Gold price
Cost inflation, Obuasi suspension

AUR.summary: Driverless trucking on Sun Belt lanes (~440k driverless miles, target >200 trucks by end-2026), but still pre-revenue scale with 2025 losses of $816M; a builder of a new market, not yet proven economics.
threats: competing autonomous truck developers (Kodiak, Plus, Waabi) and regulation
innovation: driverless freight-as-a-service on Texas-Phoenix lanes; driver-as-a-service planned 2027

AVGO.summary: Custom AI XPUs (Google TPU, Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic) are a new market: Q3 AI semi revenue $16.7B, +221% YoY, FY26 AI target ~$58B.
innovation: custom AI accelerators / XPUs
AI networking

B.summary: Gold miner; revenue follows gold (~$4,300/oz vs $4,500 company assumption). No technology obsolescence; North American IPO delayed to 2027.

BMY.summary: Not tech obsolescence: Opdivo and Eliquis (~45-50% of revenue) lose US exclusivity around 2028; the bridge depends on Cobenfy, milvexian and ~10 launches by 2030, so revenue erosion is scheduled but not yet showing.
threats: Opdivo/Eliquis loss of exclusivity ~2028 (generics/biosimilars)
Cobenfy and milvexian readout risk
innovation: Cobenfy (new-mechanism schizophrenia drug, $2-10B peak estimates)
Camzyos, Breyanzi growth

CBOE.summary: Gains from the shift to short-dated options (SPX 0DTE, ~200k contracts/day per Cboe) and is extending into event/binary contracts to meet Kalshi/Polymarket-style demand; prediction markets are also a competitor for that retail flow.
threats: prediction-market platforms (Kalshi, Polymarket) competing for retail event-risk flow
innovation: SPX 0DTE options; planned all-or-nothing/event contracts tied to SPX (launch status unverified)

CDNS.summary: EDA leader gaining from AI chip design demand (Q2 revenue +24% to $1.58B, FY26 growth guide raised to 19%); AI-driven design tools extend the moat rather than replace it. No sign AI startups or in-house tools are taking share.
threats: AI-native design tools / in-house EDA at hyperscalers (risk only, not visible)
innovation: AI-assisted chip design and system-analysis tools

CEG.summary: Largest US nuclear fleet owner selling existing/uprated carbon-free output to hyperscalers under 20-year PPAs; a trend beneficiary, not an innovator creating a new market.
threats: Crane (Three Mile Island) restart depends on NRC approvals; PJM transmission upgrades not expected until Dec 2030 (FERC waiver granted)
No named technology displacing its fleet; no evidence of share or pricing loss
innovation: Google 20-year PPA for 890 MW from uprates at existing plants (announced 2026-10-06; >$4.3B investment, first uprate 2028)
Microsoft 20-year PPA for the restarted Crane unit

CRCL.summary: Stablecoins are a growing market and USDC (~$78B, ~25% share) grows faster than USDT, but the GENIUS Act opens the field to banks and consortia (Open USD: Stripe/Coinbase/Visa/BlackRock); USDC share fell from 34% (2022); reserve income is rate-sensitive and shared with Coinbase.
threats: Bank-issued and consortium stablecoins after the GENIUS Act
Lower rates cut reserve income
Coinbase revenue share
innovation: Regulated dollar stablecoin for US institutions (OCC trust charter July 2026)

CRDO.summary: Invented the active electrical cable (AEC) market for AI data centers and holds ~88% of it (650 Group); Jefferies sees AEC units 8.6M in 2026 to 12.3M in 2027.
threats: Marvell Alaska AECs with Amphenol; Broadcom/Astera Labs
co-packaged optics longer term (timing uncertain; Jefferies calls it a non-factor near term)
innovation: AECs for scale-up AI clusters; ZeroFlap optics and active LED cables

CRWD.summary: Endpoint security leader adding AI-agent security; Microsoft Defender/Security Copilot bundling is the standing competitive threat (CEO: 'Microsoft is always going to be a competitor'), not obsolescence. Evidence on new-market creation is thin.
threats: Microsoft Defender and Security Copilot bundling
Palo Alto Networks platformization
innovation: AI agent security and AI red-teaming

CSCO.summary: AI networking shift is lifting it: FY2026 hyperscaler AI infrastructure orders $9.3B (~4.5x FY25), ~$4B AI revenue, guiding ~$7.5B in FY2027; FY26 revenue $63.3B +12%.
threats: Arista and white-box/NVIDIA Spectrum-X in AI data-center networking
innovation: hyperscaler AI back-end networking: $9.3B orders in FY2026

CVS.summary: Turnaround led by Aetna margin recovery (MLR 87.4% vs 89.9%); 2026 EPS guide raised twice to $7.90-8.10. PBM business-model transition flagged as a 2027 headwind; no clear tech obsolescence found in this check.
threats: PBM reform / cost-plus models (Mark Cuban Cost Plus) and drug-price deals squeezing Caremark
online pharmacy (Amazon) pressure on retail scripts (not quantified here)

DDOG.summary: Gains from AI workloads: LLM Observability spans up ~10x and Bits AI SRE GA with 1,000+ paying customers; FY26 revenue guide raised to ~$4.3B (+25-27%). Risk: hyperscaler native monitoring and Dynatrace/Cisco-Splunk competition.
threats: hyperscaler native monitoring (AWS/Azure/GCP) at lower cost
Dynatrace and Cisco/Splunk expanding observability
innovation: LLM / AI-agent observability and GPU monitoring

DELL.summary: AI server builder: record AI backlog ($43B at FY26 end, reported ~$51B later), demand ahead of supply; PC side flat to down. Gains from the AI build-out but on lower-margin pass-through hardware.
threats: Low-margin AI server mix and DRAM cost inflation
Hyperscalers buying direct from ODMs
Weak consumer PC demand
innovation: AI factory / rack-scale server systems
AI PCs

FCEL.summary: On-site data-center power is a real new market (4 GW proposal pipeline, ~89% data-center), but FCEL is a small, unprofitable player well behind Bloom Energy (2 GW capacity, Oracle 2.8 GW deal); thin evidence it wins share.
threats: Bloom Energy's scale lead in data-center fuel cells; Plug Power entering
innovation: standardized 12.5 MW fuel-cell blocks for data-center on-site power; ~4 GW proposal pipeline

FNV.summary: Gold/oil royalty and streaming company; revenue follows commodity prices (Q2 2026 revenue +57% YoY on higher gold). No technology making the royalty model obsolete.

GOOG.summary: AI could erode classic search, but AI Overviews (2B+ users), Gemini app (750M+ MAU), Cloud +63% with $460B backlog and Waymo (500k rides/wk) show it is gaining. Capex guide $195-205B, FCF turned negative in a quarter.
threats: AI answer engines vs classic search
innovation: Gemini
Google Cloud TPUs
Waymo

GOOGL.summary: AI chatbots (ChatGPT, others) are the named threat to search, but Google traffic still grew (+4% y/y daily visits, June) and Gemini passed ~950M MAU; Cloud is the growth engine (+63% y/y Q1 2026). Gains from the shift so far.
threats: Generative AI answer engines (OpenAI ChatGPT) taking query share; Similarweb put Gemini at ~18% vs ChatGPT ~68% of chatbot web traffic, Jan 2026
innovation: Gemini app ~950M monthly users (Q2 2026 call, secondary source)
Google Cloud AI infrastructure, +63% y/y to $20B in Q1 2026

HOOD.summary: Prediction-market event contracts (+320% to $147M in Q1 2026) and the 'everything app' push offset a 47% crypto-revenue drop; the named threat (AI and broker cash-balance worries) is a sentiment concern so far, with no visible share loss.
threats: AI-driven trading/advice tools and pressure on broker cash-sweep income (named by Morgan Stanley, Oct 2026)
crypto-cycle dependence
innovation: prediction markets / event contracts: 8.8B contracts traded in Q1 2026

HPQ.summary: Printing (its high-margin profit pool) is in structural decline (supplies and hardware volumes falling); the AI-PC refresh helps the PC side but memory costs have roughly doubled in the bill of materials. Not yet collapsing: tank printers +42%.
threats: paperless workflows shrinking print supplies
memory cost inflation squeezing PC margins
innovation: AI PCs expected ~50% of shipments by end of FY2026

IAG.summary: Gold producer: revenue follows the gold price; Cote Gold ramp (conveyor and second cone crusher fixed, near full capacity in June) and FY guide 720-820koz on track. No technology obsolescence angle.
threats: Gold price
Operational ramp risk at Cote

INCY.summary: Profitable JAK franchise; Jakafi loses exclusivity ~2028 (generic/next-gen JAK competition, not a tech shift); Jakafi XR and Opzelura (EU CHMP positive, moderate AD) are the offsets.
threats: Jakafi loss of exclusivity ~2028 (~$3B patent cliff by 2029)
novel JAK inhibitors competing with Jakafi (RBC physician survey)
innovation: Opzelura topical ruxolitinib, 2026 sales guided $750-790M
Jakafi XR once-daily reformulation

INTC.summary: AMD has taken PC and server CPU share (server ~30%) and Arm designs keep gaining; offset is 18A foundry (yields ~85% per KeyBanc, outside customers reported, break-even pulled forward). Core x86 franchise still losing ground.
threats: AMD EPYC/Ryzen share gains
Arm-based CPUs in PCs and data centers
TSMC process lead
innovation: 18A/14A foundry for outside customers

IONQ.summary: Building the commercial quantum computing market: Q2 2026 revenue $80.1M (+287% YoY), FY26 guide raised to $280-290M, $470M backlog; peers (Rigetti, D-Wave, QUBT) each under $5M/quarter. Still loss-making and acquisitive (SkyWater, all-stock Elisity deal up to $1.3B is dilutive).
threats: Big-tech quantum programs (IBM, Google) and superconducting rivals
dilution from all-stock acquisitions
innovation: Trapped-ion systems (AQ 64 Tempo, 99.99% 2-qubit fidelity)
quantum networking / security via acquisitions

ISRG.summary: da Vinci 5 (force feedback, efficiency) drives a replacement cycle; 2026 procedure growth guided 13.5-15.5%; no technology making robotic surgery obsolete, rivals (Medtronic Hugo, J&J Ottava) still small.
threats: Competing surgical robots (Medtronic Hugo, J&J Ottava) entering the US
Softer deferrable US procedures (US growth 12% in Q2)
innovation: da Vinci 5 with force feedback
Expansion of robotic procedures into new categories and international markets

JNJ.summary: Stelara is eroding ~55-60% to biosimilars, but Tremfya (+71%) and the oncology franchise offset it; 2026 sales guide $100.3-101.3B. A patent cliff, not a technology making the business obsolete.
threats: Stelara biosimilars
talc litigation and China risk
innovation: Tremfya, Icotyde, Carvykti/Tecvayli/Talvey/Rybrevant oncology launches

KEYS.summary: AI data-center build-out made wireline test overtake wireless; FQ3 revenue +36%, orders +56%, FY26 growth raised to high-20s%; 6G/AI-RAN/NTN validation is an early new market.
threats: Supply-chain limits on converting orders
Cyclical test-equipment demand if AI capex slows
innovation: AI data-center interconnect and 1.6T test
Early 6G, AI-RAN and non-terrestrial network validation

KLAC.summary: Process-control leader riding AI and advanced-packaging demand (June-quarter revenue ~$3.66B, +15% y/y; guide ~$4.0B). Gains from the shift; no new untapped market of its own.
threats: Chinese domestic equipment makers (risk, mostly in other tool types)
innovation: Inspection/metrology for advanced packaging and HBM

LITE.summary: Lumentum's lasers and optical circuit switches are building the optical layer of AI data centers; OCS backlog >$400M (Google a key customer) and co-packaged optics moving from evaluation to booked orders into 2027. Demand exceeds supply.
threats: customer concentration
capacity constraints (EML shortfall ~25-30%)
competition in transceivers
innovation: optical circuit switching (OCS) for AI clusters
co-packaged optics lasers
EML/indium phosphide capacity

LRCX.summary: Etch/deposition leader benefiting from AI and memory tightness (RBC, Apr 2026); China exposure falling as global spend rises. Chinese etch makers (AMEC, Naura) are a share risk inside China, not yet visible in results.
threats: AMEC / Naura gaining domestic China etch share
innovation: Etch and deposition for HBM and gate-all-around chips

MA.summary: Positioning to own agentic and stablecoin rails rather than be bypassed: Agent Pay / Agent Pay for Machines (June 2026, cards + A2A + stablecoins), BVNK stablecoin infrastructure deal (~$1.8B, Mar 2026), instant clearing. Open stablecoin protocols (x402) are the bypass risk; card volumes still rising.
threats: Open-protocol stablecoin rails (x402) and account-to-account payments bypassing card networks
innovation: Agent Pay for Machines
BVNK stablecoin settlement
instant clearing

MCO.summary: AI-model and private-credit 'disintermediation' fears hit the stock in early 2026, but private-credit ratings revenue grew >80% YoY in Q1 and AI data-center debt drove record issuance; regulatory moat intact. Risk named, not visible in results.
threats: AI credit models / analytics substitutes (narrative so far, not in share)
private credit moving issuance off public markets
innovation: private-credit ratings (+80% YoY Q1 2026); AI data-center financing issuance

META.summary: AI glasses are a new device category Meta dominates (~76% of 2025 smart-glasses shipments per IDC); the core ad business is growing (+26%), and the open question is the return on its capex.
threats: AI assistants competing for attention and ad dollars (a risk so far)
return on $135B+ capex unproven
innovation: Ray-Ban/Oakley Meta glasses, 7M+ sold in 2025
Ray-Ban Display supply-limited
AI ad tools

MNST.summary: Still a top-2 energy-drink brand (~27% per Circana vs Red Bull ~36%); Celsius+Alani Nu (~20%) are taking share in the low-sugar/wellness segment, but Monster revenue grew ~20% YoY in Q2 2026, so share pressure is not yet visible in results.
threats: Celsius/Alani Nu low-sugar 'better-for-you' energy drinks

MOD.summary: Data-center cooling grew 73% to >$1.1B (35% of FY2026 sales) with a $4B+ 2027-29 capacity agreement; a warm-water-cooling threat to chillers exists but has not shown up in demand.
threats: Nvidia said (CES, Jan 2026) Vera Rubin can run on 45C water 'with no chillers necessary'; MOD fell ~7-15% that day. Experts (Dell'Oro) say it reduces, not eliminates, chillers and may shift spend to dry coolers. Not yet visible: FY2027 data-center guide +60-80%
Customer concentration in hyperscaler capex cycle
innovation: Data-center cooling (Airedale chillers, CDUs/liquid cooling) for AI build-out: +73% to >$1.1B in FY2026
Long-term capacity agreement for >$4B of data-center cooling products 2027-2029 ($165M prepaid)
Exiting legacy auto-oriented Performance Technologies via Gentherm transaction to focus on data centers/HVAC

MPWR.summary: Power-management chips riding the AI data-center buildout: Q2 revenue +47.6% YoY to a record $981M, Enterprise Data growth floor raised to 130% for 2026.
threats: high-power AI rack designs could favor vertically integrated suppliers; competition from Infineon/Vicor in 48V power
innovation: AI server/accelerator power delivery (Enterprise Data segment growth floor 130% in 2026)

MRVL.summary: Rides the AI data-center shift through optical interconnect (1.6T optics in volume production, guided +50% for FY2027) and 18 custom-chip programs; risk is losing custom-chip sockets (most Amazon Trainium 3 went to Alchip). Gains from the shift; not creating a new market.
threats: losing custom XPU sockets to Broadcom/Alchip (Trainium 3)
innovation: 1.6T optical interconnect; co-packaged optics via Celestial AI (revenue from 2028)

MU.summary: HBM/server memory for AI lifted Micron to ~23% of DRAM revenue (TrendForce Q2 2026), near SK hynix; the gain is from the AI shift, not a new market it created.
threats: CXMT, the fastest-growing DRAM supplier (~7-10% share), expanding into HBM/LPDDR6
HBM3E price declines and HBM4 timing
innovation: HBM for AI accelerators; server memory mix

NBIS.summary: GPU neocloud building a new AI-compute market: Q2 2026 revenue $582M (+454% y/y), ~$27B Meta contract, 2026 guide $3.0-3.4B; risks are hyperscaler competition, commoditization and $20-25B capex/leverage.
threats: hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) and other neoclouds (CoreWeave, Lambda) commoditizing GPU capacity
execution on $20-25B capex
innovation: purpose-built AI cloud for training/inference; demand exceeds supply; ~$27B multi-year Meta deal

NBIX.summary: Ingrezza (tardive dyskinesia) still growing ~17% vs Teva Austedo; Crenessity opened the CAH treatment market, H1 2026 sales $337M (~5x YoY). Risks: Austedo Medicare price cut 2027, Crinetics atumelnant in CAH.
threats: Teva Austedo/Austedo XR in TD and HD chorea
Crinetics atumelnant (CAH)
Medicare price negotiation
innovation: Crenessity: first-in-class CRF1 antagonist for congenital adrenal hyperplasia

NEM.summary: Largest gold producer; results follow the gold price, no technology shift threatens or expands its market.

NET.summary: Moving from CDN/security into infrastructure for AI agents (agent runtime, Agent Memory, AI Search, Workers AI inference at the edge); revenue ~+34% YoY. Competes with AWS, Google, Akamai, Fastly, Vercel on this; gains from the shift. Sources are thin secondary coverage.
threats: AWS Bedrock Agents
Google Vertex AI
Akamai
Fastly
Vercel
innovation: edge AI agent runtime and inference

NOW.summary: AI agents threaten seat-based licensing (fewer human users per customer); stock ~35% down in 2026, but subscription revenue still +22% (Q1 2026), so the risk is not yet in the numbers; NOW is moving to usage/outcome pricing and an agent platform (Anthropic partnership).
threats: AI agents reduce seat counts
Agent platforms from hyperscalers and model labs bypassing workflow software
innovation: Usage/outcome-based pricing
AI agent workflow layer built on its platform

NVDA.summary: Still the dominant AI accelerator supplier; hyperscaler custom ASICs (Broadcom, Marvell, Google TPU) are the named threat and growing fastest, but estimates put ASICs at only ~13% of accelerator sales by 2027. Gains from the AI shift; share-erosion risk, not obsolescence.
threats: custom ASICs/XPUs from Broadcom and Marvell for hyperscalers
in-house chips (Google TPU, Amazon Trainium, Meta)
AMD MI-series
innovation: AI data-center accelerators and the CUDA software ecosystem

OKLO.summary: Pre-revenue advanced-fission developer targeting a new data-center power market; real customer interest but no NRC license yet, so innovating, not proven disruptor.
threats: Licensing/execution risk: NRC only approved the Principal Design Criteria topical report (Apr 2026); Aurora still in NRC pre-application, Aurora-INL proceeding under DOE authorization, startup targeted ~2028
Competing SMR/advanced-reactor developers chase the same hyperscaler offtake; Switch (12 GW) and Equinix (500 MW) agreements are non-binding
No sign of share/pricing loss: the stock decline (~-61% YTD) reflects timeline/valuation, not obsolescence
innovation: Aurora powerhouse (small fast reactor) for data-center and industrial power: a new, largely untapped market for on-site/dedicated advanced nuclear
Customer pipeline: Switch 12 GW master power agreement (non-binding), Equinix 500 MW LOI; reported Meta prepayment for a 1.2 GW Ohio campus (single-sourced)
Aurora Fuel Fabrication Facility at INL for first-core fuel

PAC.summary: Mexican airport operator (12 airports + Jamaica); September traffic -6.7% YoY on airline seat cuts and Hurricane Polo, Q2 network traffic -5.6%. A cyclical/demand dip, not a technology threat; terminal expansion and tariff increases planned.
threats: airline capacity cuts
Jamaica traffic after Hurricane Melissa
jet fuel costs
innovation: 55% terminal expansion by 2029

PANW.summary: Platformization plus AI security products (AI Access, AI Runtime Security, AI-SPM) position it to gain from vendor consolidation; AI-native rivals (CrowdStrike, Zscaler, Wiz) are pushing into the same space, so margin pressure is the risk, not obsolescence.
threats: AI-native security rivals (CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Wiz, Zscaler) competing on AI detection
innovation: securing enterprise AI adoption and agents; platform consolidation toward $15B ARR target

PAYX.summary: SMB payroll/HR is compliance-heavy and sticky; Paychex is adopting AI itself (~500-600 Wise AI features) rather than being replaced by it; growth steps down to 5-6% in FY27 after the Paycor deal, with synergies ahead of plan. No visible share loss.
threats: AI-native/cloud HCM rivals (Gusto, Rippling, ADP) pressuring SMB pricing
Small-business employment slowdown
innovation: Agentic AI compliance/productivity tools (possible future monetization)

PNC.summary: No visible technology disruption: PNC is consolidating (FirstBank closed Jan 2026, +$850-900M NII) to compete at national scale; fintech and deposit competition are background pressures, not showing in results.
threats: deposit competition from larger banks and fintechs
innovation: national expansion via acquisition and branch build-out

PSA.summary: Self-storage has no technology substitute; the threat is new entrants using cheap cloud/AI pricing tools, which favors scale players like PSA (NSA and PS Canada deals closed 2026, move-in rents +9% in Q3).
threats: new entrants using cloud management and AI dynamic pricing
muted moving-driven demand while mortgage rates stay high
innovation: AI revenue management and digital rental at scale

QCOM.summary: Losing Apple's modem business (~$5.7B+/yr at risk by 2027) but replacing it with data-center AI chips (Amazon deal of up to $60B, target $15B DC revenue by FY2029) and record automotive; the core handset business is being substituted, not made obsolete.
threats: Apple in-house modems replacing Qualcomm (already happening)
innovation: AI data-center inference chips (Amazon partnership)
automotive silicon at a record ~$1.33B per quarter

RBRK.summary: Cyber-resilience leader extending into AI-agent governance and recovery (Rubrik Agent Cloud, Bedrock/Copilot/Gemini integrations); cloud ARR +57%; rivals CrowdStrike and Palo Alto compete in AI security.
threats: CrowdStrike and Palo Alto platform consolidation
Growth decelerating from peak; still loss-making on GAAP
innovation: Rubrik Agent Cloud: monitor, govern and roll back AI agent actions

RDDT.summary: Two-sided: Google AI Overviews and LLM answers cut search referral clicks (YouTube overtook Reddit as most-cited AI source), but Reddit sells its human conversation data to Google/OpenAI and revenue still grew ~61%. Not visible in revenue yet.
threats: Google AI Overviews reducing search referrals
YouTube overtaking Reddit as AI-answer source (16% vs 10% of LLM citations)
innovation: AI data-licensing (Google, OpenAI)
Reddit Answers AI search

RGLD.summary: Gold royalty/streaming company; revenue roughly doubled YoY with gold prices (company financials). Business model faces no technology disruption; results follow the metal price.

RMBS.summary: Memory-interface chips and IP (DDR5 RCD, MRDIMM, HBM controller IP) gain from AI-server memory bandwidth demand; no technology displacing it found. Revenue +20%, ~33% net margin.
threats: memory module cycle; larger chip vendors in interface chips
innovation: DDR5/MRDIMM server memory chips
HBM4 controller IP

ROST.summary: Off-price store chain gaining share from value-seeking shoppers (Deutsche Bank sees +210 bp off-price share in 2026); no sign online retail is eroding the treasure-hunt model, and no new market either.
threats: online discount marketplaces (risk only, not visible in results)

SCCO.summary: A low-cost copper producer gaining from demand for electrification and AI data centers in a supply deficit; it has no innovation of its own, and aluminum substitution is a risk only at high copper prices.
threats: aluminum substitution in HVAC and wiring
800V DC power and optics using less copper per data center
innovation: benefits from ~475kt of 2026 data-center copper demand (JPM) and a refined-copper deficit

SKHY.summary: AI memory leader: HBM supplier to Nvidia-class accelerators; rides the AI build-out rather than being displaced by it. Risk is memory-cycle pricing, not obsolescence.
threats: memory price cycle; Samsung/Micron HBM4 competition
innovation: HBM / HBM4 for AI accelerators (~50%+ share reported)

SLB.summary: Core oilfield services shrinking (Q2 rev -4.5% YoY, Middle East disruption) while Data Center Solutions grew 63% in 1H26 (Meta 1GW Canada project, ~$3.4B Kelvion cooling deal) and digital ARR >$1B. Diversifying, but still mostly an oil-cycle business.
threats: Oil-capex cycle and Middle East activity
innovation: Data center infrastructure and cooling
Digital/AI subsurface software

SNDK.summary: AI-inference demand for NAND (model storage, KV-cache) is lifting the flash market; Sandisk gains, and its own new market (HBF) is still pre-sample.
threats: NAND commodity boom-bust cycle
Chinese NAND capacity additions
innovation: HBF high-bandwidth flash, OCP spec with SK hynix, first die taped out, samples 2027
high-endurance AI inference SSDs

SNOW.summary: Databricks is pulling ahead in the AI data-platform race (~$6.9B ARR +80% vs Snowflake ~$5.3B +34%, mid-2026, Tunguz), with ~25% of Databricks ARR from AI; Snowflake product revenue still +31% (Q2 FY27) and its AI layer (Cortex, Snowflake Intelligence) is small. Share loss, not yet shrinking.
threats: Databricks
hyperscaler data platforms
innovation: Snowflake Intelligence
Cortex Code

SPCX.summary: Starlink is the disruptor in broadband/satellite connectivity: ~12M subscribers at 2026-06-30 (about 2x y/y), connectivity revenue ~$4.3B in Q2 2026 (+~66% y/y); rivals are years behind.
threats: Amazon Leo (Kuiper) is the main challenger but had only ~390 satellites in orbit by July 2026 vs ~10,000+ for Starlink; commercial service only starting late 2026
ARPU falling (~$85 to ~$66/month) as growth shifts to cheaper markets: a pricing trend, not obsolescence
Heavy AI-related capex weighed on the first post-IPO quarter (stock -~8% after hours, Aug 2026)
innovation: Starlink LEO broadband displacing rural DSL/legacy GEO satellite and serving markets wireline never reached (12.0M subs, Q2 2026)
Direct-to-cell satellite service (reported >6M monthly users per PitchBook; revenue not disclosed)
Reusable launch (Falcon) and Starship lowering cost per kg to orbit

SPG.summary: E-commerce is the long-standing structural risk to malls, but Q2 2026 occupancy held 96%, base rent +6.3%, new-deal rents +17% and 2026 FFO guide was raised; Class-A malls are taking share from weaker centers rather than being made obsolete.
threats: continued e-commerce penetration shrinking the tenant pool
innovation: mixed-use/dining redevelopment of premium centers

STX.summary: AI data-center nearline HDD demand (HAMR/Mozaic high-capacity drives) with capacity sold out through 2026; risk is Toshiba doubling AI-HDD capacity by FY2027 (pricing) and long-run flash substitution.
threats: Toshiba plans to double AI data-center HDD capacity by FY2027 (supply/pricing risk)
QLC flash SSDs substituting HDDs at the high end over time
innovation: HAMR high-capacity nearline drives for AI/cloud storage

TEM.summary: AI precision-oncology platform; testing builds a proprietary multimodal data moat that grows more valuable as AI and biomarker-driven therapy spread; ~25% revenue growth guided for 2026. Not yet profitable; rivals (Guardant, Foundation Medicine, Caris) not quantified.
threats: Large diagnostics rivals in genomic testing
AI models commoditising if data access widens
innovation: Multimodal oncology foundation models
Data licensing to pharma

TER.summary: Semiconductor test demand from AI compute/HBM drove revenue +104% YoY; robotics (UR/MiR) is a smaller optional new market. No obsolescence threat found; recent drops are sector selling.
innovation: AI accelerator and HBM test systems
collaborative robots (Universal Robots)

TROW.summary: Active mutual-fund manager losing assets to passive index funds; net outflows continue in 2026 (Q2 -$6.5B; reports of ~$28B in Q3) and fee rate is slipping (38.1 bps). Active-ETF push ($30B AUM) is the offset.
threats: shift from active funds to low-cost passive index funds and ETFs
passive/blend target-date funds taking share
innovation: active ETF platform (34 funds, $30B AUM)

TSM.summary: Leading-edge foundry that makes most AI accelerators; extends current EUV through several nodes instead of buying High-NA early. No technology named that makes its business obsolete; the main risks are geopolitical and customer concentration, not disruption.
threats: Intel/Samsung adopting High-NA EUV earlier could narrow the process lead (not visible yet)
innovation: Sole volume supplier of leading-edge AI accelerators; 2026 capex plan ~$52-56B per one analysis

UI.summary: Enterprise Technology grew ~32% in FY26 to ~$2.97B by selling a unified stack (Protect cameras, Access door readers, Talk phones, cloud gateways) to SMB/prosumer IT at prices below Cisco/HPE; component cost inflation is the near-term margin risk.
threats: Cisco/HPE Aruba/cloud-managed rivals
Component cost inflation and supply constraints
innovation: Unified, subscription-free physical security + networking for small/mid enterprises

UMC.summary: Mature-node foundry: record Q3 2026 shipments (>1.2M 12-inch eq.), utilization 92%, revenue +25.6% YoY, plus US$3.2B more capex for Singapore/Tainan. Not creating a new market; mature nodes face Chinese foundry price competition.
threats: Chinese mature-node foundries (SMIC, Hua Hong) adding capacity and pressuring prices
innovation: capacity expansion in Singapore and Tainan for specialty/mature-node demand

USB.summary: Large regional bank; fintech competition in payments is a noted risk, and it is responding with a USBDC stablecoin pilot on Stellar (first live cross-border transfer Sept 2026) and stablecoin-reserve custody for Anchorage. No visible obsolescence; not creating a new market.
threats: fintechs in core payments
stablecoin payment rails
innovation: USBDC stablecoin pilot
stablecoin reserve custody

VLO.summary: Refining margins very strong in 2026 (Q2 refining op income $4.5B vs $1.3B; $23.62/bbl), and Diamond Green Diesel renewable diesel/SAF swung to $717M profit. Long-run EV adoption erodes gasoline demand; not visible in current numbers. Oil sector is de-emphasized for new entries per Ryan's steer.
threats: EV adoption eroding long-run gasoline demand
credit-dependent renewable diesel economics
innovation: Diamond Green Diesel renewable diesel and SAF (~1.2B gal/yr)

VRTX.summary: Cystic fibrosis franchise plus newer markets (non-opioid pain, gene editing); a 2025 phase-2 pain-drug failure cut the pain upside, so it gains from new therapies but has not yet proven a large new market.
threats: Pipeline setbacks in pain (2025 phase-2 failure)
innovation: Non-opioid pain (Journavx), CRISPR gene therapy

VST.summary: Incumbent nuclear + gas generator riding data-center demand through long-term contracts; a beneficiary of the AI power trend, not itself disrupting or being disrupted.
threats: Regulatory: Texas/ERCOT pause on new data-center interconnection (management supports it; says the 1.2 GW Amazon Comanche Peak deal is unaffected)
No named technology currently displacing its nuclear/gas fleet; no evidence of share or pricing loss
innovation: 20-year PPA with Amazon for 1,200 MW from Comanche Peak (deliveries from Q4 2027, full by 2032)
20-year agreements with Meta for 2,609 MW from PJM nuclear incl. ~433 MW of uprates; DOE conditional loan up to $4.2B (2026-10-05) for uprates/life extension
Gas expansion: Cogentrix (~5,500 MW) acquisition, 860 MW new Permian units

WDC.summary: AI data-lake build-out made nearline HDDs scarce: sold out for 2026, LTAs into 2027-28, 26TB CMR/32TB UltraSMR ramp, HAMR in hyperscale qualification for 2027; flash substitution is a long-run risk but SSDs cost ~16x per TB.
threats: QLC flash SSDs replacing nearline HDD if $/TB gap closes
Seagate HAMR lead; Toshiba doubling AI HDD capacity (pricing discipline)
innovation: AI training/inference data storage at exabyte scale (190 EB shipped in FQ4)

WES.summary: Permian midstream, 2026 EBITDA guide raised to $2.75-2.95B (Brazos Delaware deal, produced-water growth). Volume follows oil and gas activity; no disruption visible.
innovation: produced-water reuse

WPM.summary: Precious-metals streamer; record Q2 2026 revenue $929M on higher prices and the Antamina silver stream. Revenue follows gold/silver, no obsolescence threat.
